newsitem.title: ITALY: INSTANT VIEW - Italy prelim Jan CPI 0.1 pct mo/mo.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Italy prelim Jan CPI 0.1 pct mo/mo.

text.p: Following are economists' reactions to the preliminary 0.1 percent month-on-month rise in Italian January consumer prices, released by the sample cities of Trieste and Turin on Monday.
The year-on-year CPI rate was seen at 2.5/2.6 percent.
Economists in a Reuters survey had forecast on average a month-on-month rate of 0.2 percent and a year-on-year rate of 2.6 percent.
Marco Pianelli European analyst at Nomura said, "This shows inflation is less than the consensus".
In December 1996, there was a month-on-month CPI rate of 0.1 percent and a year-on-year rate of 2.6 percent. On Tuesday, a further nine Italian cities will reported their CPI data.
Maria Rosa Trolese, analyst at Deutsche Bank in Milan, said they were looking to see 0.1 percent month-on-month rate and 2.5 percent year-on-year in January.
"But we need to see the other cities' figures. Two cities on their own mean little," she added.

Lorenzo Stanca, head of research of Credito Italiano, said that the Bank of Italy will probably want to see good inflation numbers and an agreement in the on-going wage dispute between employers and metalworkers before cutting interest rates.

Analysts said that a wage accord was critical for the timing of a rate cut, but even if there was no wage accord there would have to be a rate cut because of the effect the high lira was having on the Italian economy.
"If we see a wage accord coming out at the end of this week, I think the Bank of Italy will clearly cut rates, probably by 0.75 percent," Nomura's Pianelli said.
